Recorded as 1943-04-30, inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day, under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling on until-dates); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption stops when that day begins, is the alternative. Actor: EO 9031 itself, whose registered held text supplies the stated term. The employee named is Edgar M. Cohee.

research_rationale:
EO 9031 (January 20, 1942, Franklin D. Roosevelt) read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-9031-exemption-edgar-m-cohee-from-compulsory-retirement-for-age.txt; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md, done 2026-11-04: the page record with the same sha256 in the APP mirror records (capture archive common-crawl) has the heading Executive Order 9031—Exemption of Edgar M. Cohee From Compulsory Retirement for Age, date 1942-01-20, and a text_sha256 equal to the held file's; the heading names this order's number and its subject agrees with the text. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the clause-drafts copy. The order (read in full, one paragraph of recital and one operative sentence) recites that the employee was exempted for one year by EO 8692 of February 21, 1941 and further exempts him for one year ending April 30, 1943; the earlier grant is an earlier instrument recited in the text, not a later event, and this order is a new exercise of the section 204 proviso with its own fixed term. First end: the order's own fixed term, recorded as 1943-04-30, inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption stops when that day begins, is the alternative. Authority: section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), cited in the order. No held source shows that section repealed or amended before the stated end; a held later exemption order (EO 9530, March 14, 1945) still cites section 204, which corroborates the authority but is not an event affecting this order.
